Import/export works with real files. Refresh **http://maker:4001** — the **Import…** and **Export** buttons are in the top-right.

**Flow 14 — import & export.**
1. Click **Export.** Your browser downloads **bookmarks.html** in the **standard browser-bookmarks format** — which you can re-import into any browser. It preserves each bookmark's **title, tags, and original saved date** (and notes). A confirmation line shows how many were exported.
2. Click **Import…** and pick a standard bookmarks HTML file (one exported from a browser, or the one you just exported). The app reads every link and adds them, **keeping titles, tags, and original saved dates** where the file provides them. A line reports how many were **added** and how many were **skipped as already in your collection** (using the same duplicate rule as saving).

I verified a round trip: exported entries carry their tags and dates, and re-importing skips ones you already have while imported tags stay searchable (e.g. `#reading`).

Two decisions to confirm:
- **Import adds to your collection and skips duplicates** (matching an already-saved page), rather than replacing anything or creating second copies. Imported items come in as ordinary (not to-read, not archived). Right behaviour?
- When a file **doesn't provide a saved date or tags** (many browser exports omit tags), I keep what's there and fill a missing date with **today**. Is "keep what's available, default the rest" what you'd expect, or should undated imports be flagged somehow?
